properties.name: When a design has just been created, the person is told two or three things they can do next, in their own terms
properties.statement:
When genesis or adopt finishes creating a design, its closing words name two or three things the person can do next, in plain words with the slash command beside each as a shortcut. For example: "see what is still open (/gaps)", "add something it needs (/req)", "see where it stands (/where)".

Anthony, 2026-09-24, about his brother's first design on flo2: "I don't think he'll know anything beyond /genesis. So I'd imagine to him, he's probably like, cool, I created a design, so what now?" And: "the same problem also affects reflow2 at the lower level for users using reflow2 like I am here." He kept this as intent from dec:idea-a-person-learns-what-to-do-next-once-they-have-a-design, option (a).

Scope and limits, from the pushback recorded on that idea:
- Only the skills that CREATE a design (genesis, adopt) end this way. A suggestion after every skill becomes noise for someone who knows them.
- Each suggestion is phrased as something the person can ASK FOR. The command is a handle, never the only way in. This does not make the person the trigger for the agent's own skill use (req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session): the agent still reaches for skills on its own. This tells a newcomer what is possible to ask.
- It reaches flo2's chat users with nothing built in flo2, because flo2 serves these skills unchanged. On Grok the person must still say "use flo2"; that line is flo2's to carry.
